themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints on streets and sidewalks spiked to 44 reports THIS WEEK, a 382% increase from the 9.1-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden deterioration in street conditions or activity levels in CD 501.
evidence: 44 noise/street-sidewalk complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.54)
No prior context or explanation evident in available data, suggesting sudden trigger
reporting_angles: What event, construction, or activity triggered the abrupt spike in street noise this week?
Are specific neighborhoods or blocks driving the complaints—e.g., near transit hubs, entertainment venues, or construction sites?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 4 reports THIS WEEK, a 1500% spike from the 0.2-complaint weekly baseline, indicating either aggressive new enforcement action or a sudden surge in illegal vending activity in St. George/Stapleton.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 8.66)
Sharp contrast suggests new policy, enforcement blitz, or localized vendor problem
reporting_angles: Has the city launched a new enforcement campaign against street vendors in CD 501 this week?
Are residents complaining about a proliferation of unlicensed vendors, or are enforcement actions themselves drawing complaints?

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints peaked at 25 reports 2 weeks ago, a 3233% surge from the 0.8-complaint baseline, representing the most statistically extreme spike in the dataset and signaling either a genuine public safety crisis or concentrated enforcement activity.
evidence: 25 drug activity complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 29.25—highest severity spike)
3233% increase is the most extreme statistical anomaly in the entire dataset
No recent news coverage or community board mention, suggesting this may be underreported or newly surfaced
reporting_angles: Did a specific event, gang activity, or supply shift trigger this dramatic spike in reported drug activity 2 weeks ago?
Which neighborhoods in CD 501 are hotspots, and are residents and local businesses coping with visible open-air drug markets?

themes_detail.label: Elevator System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints surged to 14 reports 2 weeks ago, a 3633% spike from the 0.4-complaint weekly average, suggesting widespread mechanical failures or safety issues in residential buildings across the district.
evidence: 14 elevator complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 19.58—second-highest severity)
3633% spike indicates either systemic failure or emergency event affecting multiple buildings
Long-running budget request for street lights and infrastructure suggests broader maintenance issues in the district
reporting_angles: Did a widespread power failure, extreme weather, or maintenance backlog disable elevators across CD 501 two weeks ago?
How many buildings remain affected, and are elderly or disabled residents trapped or isolated?

themes_detail.label: Smoking/Vaping Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Smoking and vaping complaints peaked at 30 reports 3 weeks ago, a 549% increase from the 4.6-complaint weekly average, potentially signaling either enforcement of indoor smoking bans or a shift in public consumption behavior.
evidence: 30 smoking/vaping complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 4.6 weekly average (z-score: 8.47)
549% spike suggests concentrated outbreak of complaints or new enforcement activity
Signal is slightly older (3 weeks) compared to other emerging issues
reporting_angles: What triggered a spike in complaints about smoking and vaping 3 weeks ago—enforcement action or resident activism?
Are specific venues, parks, or residential buildings driving most complaints?
